checked_by: Project maintainer, with AI research assistance (see docs/research-log.md)
notes: Every external link on the site must appear here. 'opened' means the document itself was read on the 'checked' date. 'linked_from' means the address came from another official source and was not opened by our tools. Kind 'state-explainer' entries are counted on the About page to support the claim that the state explains the rules across more than a dozen documents.

sources.title: How will providers be affected by federal changes to Oregon Health Plan (OHP)? (HR1 provider FAQ)

sources.notes: Timeline, ways to meet the rules, medical exemptions, retroactive coverage, renewals, Healthier Oregon and Open Card. Contains a sentence about a work-limit test that tracks a clause a federal court vacated on Oct. 29, 2026 (see docs/corrections.md, item 1).

sources.title: Medicaid Program; Community Engagement Requirement for Certain Individuals (interim final rule), 91 Fed. Reg. 33348
sources.short: Federal rule on the work requirement (91 Fed. Reg. 33348)
sources.notes: Read the first fifth of the document (preamble sections I to II.C.8). Source for the $580 income test (not less than $7.25 times 80, household income), half-time school including high school and GED programs, what counts as work and community service, and the credit-hour conversion.

sources.title: Order of Vacatur and Enjoinment, Commonwealth of Massachusetts v. Oz, No. 1:26-cv-12962 (D. Mass. Oct. 29, 2026), Doc. 148
sources.publisher: U.S. District Court for the District of Massachusetts (via CourtListener)
sources.notes: Vacates the federal rule's medically frail clause tied to ability to comply; enjoins applying it to plaintiff states; bars penalizing plaintiff states for implementation errors or delays for six months. No later docket entries seen in CourtListener on Nov. 2, 2026.
